title: Hover-probe snapshot mode and ARIA fragmentation for time-series charts
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Our dense time-series charts create noisy accessibility announcements and high-frequency DOM updates when users hover and scrub. On slow devices or low-power modes this leads to janky hover tooltips, inconsistent screen reader behavior, and wasted work when the pointer moves rapidly across dense series.

Goal: Design a hover 'snapshot' interaction model that reduces reflow and DOM churn while delivering concise, meaningful ARIA announcements. Introduce an "ARIA fragmentation" strategy that only announces contextually important changes (new series, threshold-crossings, or user-requested details) rather than every sample under the cursor. Ensure the solution is configurable by engineers (debounce windows, priority thresholds) and documented for implementers and QA.
proposals: Snapshot mode: collect probe events on pointermove into a short sliding window (default 120ms). Only render / update tooltip DOM at window flush times to avoid per-pixel updates.

ARIA fragmentation: synthesize an announcement payload with three layers: (1) concise header (time + primary value), (2) priority changes (alerts, threshold breaches, selected series) and (3) optional detail list toggled by a keyboard action (Enter or a 'more details' control). Screen readers receive fragments in that order; only fragments that changed since last announce are emitted.

Priority rules: if multiple series change and one crosses a configured critical threshold, that series becomes the primary focus for the announcement. Non-critical series are grouped under "+N other series" to reduce verbosity.
Visual fallback: on extremely low-power devices (detected by user agent hints) fall back to a static summary overlay with a single aggregated value and 'expand' control to reveal details on demand.
Developer controls: CSS class hooks for off-main rendering, config for debounce window, threshold definitions, and ARIA attributes (aria-live region id, data-announce-fragment).
Performance targets: reduce hover-induced main-thread time by at least 50% in 95th percentile across a 20-series chart with 10k points each; keep SR announcement length to <3 lines in common cases.
decisions: Use a short debounce window (default 120ms) rather than strict per-frame updates to balance responsiveness and CPU savings.
Implement ARIA fragmentation as an ordered queue of strings emitted to a single polite aria-live region to preserve SR ordering and avoid spamming.
Group low-priority series into a collapsed summary when more than 3 series are under the probe to limit verbosity.
Expose the key knobs to engineers via config (debounceMs, priorityThresholds, collapsedCount) and document defaults in the design system tokens guide.
Prototype using an off-main canvas + lightweight DOM overlay pattern; full off-main rendering for charts will be a follow-up ENG ticket.
tasks: Create Figma flows showing probe window timing, collapsed series UI, and keyboard 'more details' path (Aisha)
Write component API surface proposal for engineers (props + aria hooks) and add to docs (Liam)
Implement prototype in playground chart with synthetic data to measure CPU and paint times (ENG-5021)
Run a11y testing matrix with VoiceOver/JAWS/ChromeVox and record announcement patterns (QA)
Add e2e tests that assert aria-live payloads and that collapsed summary appears for >3 series (QA)
Performance bench and update Optimize recommendations if snapshot mode changes token cost model (Performance team)
Document accessibility rationale and include snippet for assistive tech users explaining 'more details' control (Docs)
Coordinate with Eng on config knobs and release gating (ENG-4963)
Ship behind feature flag and run dogfood with internal dashboards for 2 weeks before GA
acceptance_criteria: Hover interactions on dense datasets update tooltip DOM at most every debounce window (configurable) and do not exceed main-thread target (measured in synthetic benchmark).
Screen reader announces only the changed ARIA fragments in order and groups low-priority series as '+N other series' when more than 3 series are present.
Keyboard-only users can expand the 'more details' fragment and navigate the values without leaving the chart canvas.
Design tokens and API surface are documented in the design system repo and include examples for low-power fallback behavior.
Prototype shows >=50% reduction in hover-related main-thread time in target benchmark compared to current baseline.
